Claire — attaching the PDF noted on my last message (redwood_verified_profiles_june2026.pdf) and a compact benchmark CSV. TL;DR on recommended model variants for your workload: 

Recommended variants (summary)
- RW-Chat-70B-8bit (recommended for best quality; quantized int8 runtime yields ~35-45% faster throughput vs fp16 on the same hardware in our tests). Expected quality: highest on clinical summarization tests.
- Llama-2-13B-chat Int8 (good balance of quality/latency; lower memory footprint, supports higher concurrent TPS).
- Mistral-7B-v0.2 Q4 (best for low-latency interactive flows where p99 is critical; modest quality drop in edge cases).

Key perf numbers from our June run (attached CSV — these are for a 600-token request profile on an A100-like instance):
- RW-Chat-70B-8bit: TPS (tokens/sec) median 920, p50 latency 120ms, p95 latency 210ms, p99 latency 350ms.
- Llama-2-13B-int8: TPS median 1500, p50 95ms, p95 150ms, p99 240ms.
- Mistral-7B-q4: TPS median 2300, p50 60ms, p95 110ms, p99 160ms.

Notes on tail latency and variance
- Tail spikes in the RW-Chat-70B profile were correlated with bursty concurrent KV cache misses in our continuous-batching runtime; we can reduce p99 by enabling aggressive prefix caching and limiting batch size for interactive routes.
- Dedicated capacity (pinned GPU pools) reduces variance vs shared hosted pools.

Attachments in this message:
- redwood_verified_profiles_june2026.pdf (contains percentile graphs, kernel selection notes, and test harness details)
- quick_benchmark_overview.csv (raw numbers)
- prompt_set_clinical_summaries_v1.txt

I also added a short guide in the Drive folder on how to run the prompt set and compute ROUGE+entity-factuality checks. Let us know if you want us to run the eval on your behalf with synthetic anonymized samples.

Best — Jordan
